messages.subject: ordinal probit model in Stan
parts:
Hi, I am trying to fit an ordinal probit model in Stan. The following is the error message. I am really confused that I did not use norma_log in my model.
Where is the error message come from and how to fix it?
 
Error message:
 
EL 'excode' FROM Stan CODE TO C++ CODE NOW.
Error in stanc(file = file, model_code = model_code, model_name = model_name,  : 
  failed to parse Stan model 'excode' with error message:
EXPECTATION FAILURE - DIAGNOSTIC(S) FROM PARSER:

no matches for function name="normal_log"
    arg 0 type=matrix
    arg 1 type=real
    arg 2 type=real
available function signatures for normal_log:
0.  normal_log(real, real, real) : real
1.  normal_log(real, real, real[1]) : real
2.  normal_log(real, real, vector) : real
3.  normal_log(real, real, row vector) : real
4.  normal_log(real, real[1], real) : real
5.  normal_log(real, real[1], real[1]) : real
6.  normal_log(real, real[1], vector) : real
7.  normal_log(real, real[1], row vector) : real
8.  normal_log(real, vector, real) : real
 
 
Code for my model:
data {
  int n; //number of subjects
  int p; //number of items
  int K[p]; //number of categories
  int Y[n,p]; //observations
  real alpha; //rho prior
  real beta; //rho prior 
  real mT; //cutpoints prior mean
  real sT; //cutpoints prior std
} 

parameters {
  vector[p] rho;
  vector[n] f;
  matrix[p,(K[p]-1)] T; 
}

model { 
  vector[p] s2;
  vector[p] s;
  matrix[p, K[p]] Tstar;
  matrix[n,p] rhof;
  real prob[n, p, K[p]];
  matrix[p,(K[p]-1)] v;
  real c[p];
  real d[p];
  real e[p];
  real g[p];
  
  f ~ normal(0,1);
  rho ~ beta(alpha, beta);
  Tstar ~ normal(mT, sT);

  for (j in 1:p) {
s2[j] <- 1-pow(rho[j],2);
      s[j] <- sqrt(s2[j]);
T[j,1:(K[j]-1)] <- sort_asc(Tstar[j,1:(K[j]-1)]);

  }

  for (i in 1:n) {
for (j in 1:p) {
rhof[i,j] <- rho[j]*f[i];
for (k in 1:(K[j]-1)) {
v[j,k] <- T[j,k]-rhof[i,j];
}
}
  }

  for (i in 1:n) {
for (j in 1:p) {
            c[j]=v[j,1];
      prob[i,j,1] <- normal_cdf(c[j],0,s[j]);
for (k in 2:(K[j]-1)) {
            d[j]=v[j,k];
            e[j]=v[j,(k-1)];
prob[i,j,k] <- normal_cdf(d[j],0,s[j]) - normal_cdf(e[j],0,s[j]);
}
            g[j]=v[j,(K[j]-1)];
prob[i,j,K[j]] <- 1-normal_cdf(g[j],0,s[j]);
}
}
 
 
Thank you so much!

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] ordinal probit model in Stan
parts: Hi Joyce,
On Sat, Aug 9, 2014 at 5:54 PM, Joyce <jian...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hi, I am trying to fit an ordinal probit model in Stan. The following is the error message. I am really confused that I did not use norma_log in my model.
Where is the error message come from and how to fix it?

The error message is coming from this line:

    Tstar ~ normal(mT, sT);

The sampling statement for the normal distribution gets translated in C++ as something like:
    increment_log_prob(normal_log(Tstar, mT, sT));

Error message:
 
EL 'excode' FROM Stan CODE TO C++ CODE NOW.
Error in stanc(file = file, model_code = model_code, model_name = model_name,  : 
  failed to parse Stan model 'excode' with error message:
EXPECTATION FAILURE - DIAGNOSTIC(S) FROM PARSER:

no matches for function name="normal_log"
    arg 0 type=matrix
    arg 1 type=real
    arg 2 type=real
available function signatures for normal_log:
0.  normal_log(real, real, real) : real
1.  normal_log(real, real, real[1]) : real
2.  normal_log(real, real, vector) : real
3.  normal_log(real, real, row vector) : real
4.  normal_log(real, real[1], real) : real
5.  normal_log(real, real[1], real[1]) : real
6.  normal_log(real, real[1], vector) : real
7.  normal_log(real, real[1], row vector) : real
8.  normal_log(real, vector, real) : real

How to fix it -- the message is telling you that the first argument, Tstar, is a matrix. Our univariate distributions don't take matrix arguments. (yet)

The easiest fix is to replace your single sampling line with this loop:

    for (i in 1:p)
       Tstar[i] ~ normal(mT, sT);

Code for my model:
data {
  int n; //number of subjects
  int p; //number of items
  int K[p]; //number of categories
  int Y[n,p]; //observations
  real alpha; //rho prior
  real beta; //rho prior 
  real mT; //cutpoints prior mean
  real sT; //cutpoints prior std
} 

parameters {
  vector[p] rho;
  vector[n] f;
  matrix[p,(K[p]-1)] T; 
}

model { 
  vector[p] s2;
  vector[p] s;
  matrix[p, K[p]] Tstar;
  matrix[n,p] rhof;
  real prob[n, p, K[p]];
  matrix[p,(K[p]-1)] v;
  real c[p];
  real d[p];
  real e[p];
  real g[p];
  
  f ~ normal(0,1);
  rho ~ beta(alpha, beta);
  Tstar ~ normal(mT, sT);

  for (j in 1:p) {
s2[j] <- 1-pow(rho[j],2);
      s[j] <- sqrt(s2[j]);
T[j,1:(K[j]-1)] <- sort_asc(Tstar[j,1:(K[j]-1)]);

  }

  for (i in 1:n) {
for (j in 1:p) {
rhof[i,j] <- rho[j]*f[i];
for (k in 1:(K[j]-1)) {
v[j,k] <- T[j,k]-rhof[i,j];
}
}
  }

  for (i in 1:n) {
for (j in 1:p) {
            c[j]=v[j,1];
      prob[i,j,1] <- normal_cdf(c[j],0,s[j]);
for (k in 2:(K[j]-1)) {
            d[j]=v[j,k];
            e[j]=v[j,(k-1)];
prob[i,j,k] <- normal_cdf(d[j],0,s[j]) - normal_cdf(e[j],0,s[j]);
}
            g[j]=v[j,(K[j]-1)];
prob[i,j,K[j]] <- 1-normal_cdf(g[j],0,s[j]);
}
}
 
 
Thank you so much!

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] ordinal probit model in Stan
parts:
First, I'd recommend using our ordered logit --- it's built
in and will be much more efficient than probit. Probit's
popular in Gibbs settings because it's easier to sample
from the conditionals. When just calculating cumulative
distributions, logit is much more efficient, as its cdf is
closed form (inverse logit).

It's more efficient to loop matrices by column, since it
preserves memory locality. So I'd recommend:

for (j in ncols)
col(mat,j) ~ ...;

It's even more efficient to redeclare the matrix as an
array of vectors, but that would then prevent matrix operations.

But there are much bigger problems in your model. See below.
The biggest problem is that you're using BUGS/JAGS/R programming
idioms that are not valid in Stan. The biggest issue here is
that we don't support the : notation for slicing arrays/matrices,
and every value has to be defined before it's used --- unlike BUGS
or JAGS (but like R), Stan executes its statements in order.

More below. I stopped after diagnosing a few problems.

> int Y[n,p]; //observations
> real alpha; //rho prior

> matrix[n,p] rhof;
> real prob[n, p, K[p]];

I don't think this is what you want. K is a vector or array
and K[p] is just one entry in it. You don't ever use any
value other than K[p] as far as I can tell.

> matrix[p,(K[p]-1)] v;
> real c[p];
> real d[p];
> real e[p];
> real g[p];
>
> f ~ normal(0,1);
> rho ~ beta(alpha, beta);
> Tstar ~ normal(mT, sT);

You can't use Tstar before you define Tstar.
So far, it's only declared. Stan executes in order.

>
> for (j in 1:p) {
> s2[j] <- 1-pow(rho[j],2);
> s[j] <- sqrt(s2[j]);
> T[j,1:(K[j]-1)] <- sort_asc(Tstar[j,1:(K[j]-1)]);
>
Stan does not support the : syntax from JAGS or BUGS or R.

> }
>
> for (i in 1:n) {
> for (j in 1:p) {
> rhof[i,j] <- rho[j]*f[i];
> for (k in 1:(K[j]-1)) {
> v[j,k] <- T[j,k]-rhof[i,j];

> prob[i,j,K[j]] <- 1-normal_cdf(g[j],0,s[j]);
> }

I don't understand all of this. Partly it's the indenting,
but the bigger issue is that you do all this work in the model and
nothing uses prob.

- Bob
